title: Measures to Prevent Patients on Kidney Dialysis from Being Discriminated against at Workplace
what_it_is: Measures to Prevent Patients on Kidney Dialysis from Being Discriminated against at Workplace

sections.label: Measures for dialysis patients at work
sections.summary: The Minister states measures to prevent workplace discrimination against dialysis patients and promote flexible work arrangements, noting 93% of firms offered FWAs in 2020.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Tan Wu Meng –  16 To ask the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the current measures to prevent dialysis patients from being discriminated against at the workplace; and (b) given the prevalence of kidney failure, what is being done to promote flexible working arrangements (FWAs) to accommodate these patients’ attendance at life-supporting dialysis centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We do so by promoting the adoption of flexible work arrangements (FWAs) and work-life strategies as well as ensuring that such employees are not discriminated against at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In 2020, 93% of firms offered some form of formal or ad hoc FWAs to employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To further entrench the implementation of such work arrangements, the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) actively promotes the Tripartite Standard on FWAs to companies through its publicity campaigns, briefings to members of trade associations and chambers (TACs) and also, conduct workshops.

sections.label: Dialysis employees protected against discrimination
sections.summary: Employees needing dialysis or with other medical conditions are protected against discrimination through the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Employees requiring dialysis treatment, or having any other medical conditions, are protected against discrimination through the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) which is based on the principles of fair and merit-based employment practices at the workplace.

sections.label: War on Diabetes and Diabetic Task Force
sections.summary: The Minister cites the War on Diabetes and Diabetic Task Force, formed years back, to manage diabetes and prevent kidney failure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I would like to check if there are any upstream measures that are implemented in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think if the Member remembers, we do have a War on Diabetes and the Diabetic Task Force has been formed a couple of years back, at least to really look at comprehensively engaging people through lifestyle changes, through exercise, through stakeholders in the community as well as in the medical fraternity, to make sure we target the management and treatment of diabetes to prevent the downstream consequences of renal impairment and kidney failure.

sections.label: Engaging employers on job redesign
sections.summary: The Minister says legislating such a requirement is challenging, and instead employers will be engaged on job redesign through the Singapore National Employers Federation and Labour Movement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Legislating a requirement like this would probably be challenging to implement because different businesses and operating models may have different needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: What we should do though is to continue to engage with our employers through the Singapore National Employers Federation as well as our Labour Movement, to continue that conversation and helping employers to look at redesigning their jobs, so that more people with disability, or even those who need flexible arrangement for dialysis treatment, can continue to be meaningfully engaged and contribute to the workforce and also to the companies' operations as well.
